summary: Create a thin board-specific application read use-case. The board policy spans two independently owned capabilities, so composing stores directly in the RSC page would put authorization and business policy in the UI, while making work-items call labels would violate change isolation. No board persistence module is needed.

tree.purpose: RSC entrypoint; obtains URL filters and calls the server-only board read entrypoint, then renders the board view.
Server-only authenticated read composition; verifies the actor, constructs trusted work-item and label readers, and invokes the board use-case.
Cross-capability orchestration: hides archived items, groups by status, requests visible label details, detects unauthorized label references, and returns a board DTO.
Board-local reader contracts for work items and labels; contains no Next.js, Supabase, or concrete adapter imports.
Existing work-items public trusted read surface; owns work-item persistence and work-item visibility rules.
Existing labels public trusted read surface; owns label persistence and actor-specific label visibility.
Server-derived actor/session verification used by the DAL and capability readers.
Pure board rendering from the serializable board DTO; no data fetching or authorization.
Optional pure board DTO/schema/status grouping helpers only; no capability persistence or framework dependencies.
Use-case tests with fake reader ports.
DAL authentication, authorization propagation, and failure mapping tests.
Rendering tests for grouped items, labels, empty states, and safe error states.
Authenticated browser flow against real data and authorization boundaries.

flows: `src/app/board/page.tsx` → `src/adapters/inbound/next/dal/get-board.ts` → verify actor/session → construct existing trusted work-item and label readers → `src/use-cases/board/get-board.ts` → work-items reader and labels reader → apply board policy → return serializable DTO → `src/ui/board/BoardView.tsx`.
The board use-case requests work items visible to the actor, removes archived items, collects referenced label IDs, and asks the labels public read surface for details visible to that same actor.

If any referenced label is not visible to the actor, the labels reader reports the authorization failure; the board use-case rejects that attachment/result rather than exposing a label name or silently treating unauthorized data as visible.

If work-item or label persistence fails, the DAL records the request/actor/error context and maps the result to a user-safe board error or route-level error boundary; raw provider exceptions and rows never reach the RSC.
Board writes, if added later, should use `Server Action → board use-case → capability command ports`, with scoped cache invalidation owned by the affected capability and board read tags.

decisions.rationale: The page must remain a thin RSC entrypoint, and neither work-items nor labels may import the other. The board is an application workflow, not a persistence owner.

decisions.choice: Board use-case depends only on board-local reader ports and domain DTOs
decisions.rationale: Concrete stores, Supabase, Next.js APIs, auth, and cache stay outside the use-case. The DAL/composition boundary injects existing capability implementations.

decisions.choice: Work-items and labels expose independent trusted read contracts
decisions.rationale: Each capability remains independently changeable and owns its persistence, mapping, visibility rules, and provider errors. The board consumes contracts rather than tables or adapters.

decisions.choice: Re-check actor authorization in the server-only DAL and each capability read boundary
decisions.rationale: Proxy/session middleware is not sufficient. Label visibility must be evaluated server-side for the current actor before details are attached.

decisions.choice: Fail closed for unauthorized label references; report infrastructure failures safely
decisions.rationale: A partial board containing ambiguous or unauthorized label data risks disclosure and inconsistent policy. Diagnostics belong in server observability, not the response.

decisions.choice: RSC plus server-only DAL owns the board read
decisions.rationale: This is a read-heavy initial page load. Avoid TanStack Query and app-internal HTTP calls; scope any cache tags by tenant/actor and invalidate them from the relevant command boundary.

decisions.choice: Test the board use-case with fake ports, adapters at their persistence boundary, and the final flow end-to-end
decisions.rationale: This verifies orchestration without coupling tests to Supabase while still covering auth, mapping, rendering, and real authorization behavior.

risks: The exact DTO and status taxonomy must align with the existing work-items public contract; do not import private persistence types.

A fail-closed policy makes one inaccessible referenced label capable of failing the board; if product requires partial rendering, return an explicit redacted-label state rather than silently dropping it.
Cache keys/tags must include tenant and actor scope when visibility is user-specific.
